function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.content:
I’m not able to see your actual connection details, but you can quickly find out your current internet speed by running an online speed test. Here’s what you can do:

1. **Open a web browser** and go to a reputable speed‑testing site such as:
   - [Speedtest by Ookla](https://www.speedtest.net/)
   - [Fast.com](https://fast.com/) (by Netflix)
   - [Google Speed Test](search “speed test” on Google and click the built‑in test)

2. **Click the “Go” or “Start” button** on the page.  
   - The test will measure your download speed, upload speed, and ping (latency).

3. **Read the results** once the test completes.  
   - Download speed is usually shown in Mbps (megabits per second).  
   - Upload speed is also shown in Mbps.  
   - Ping is shown in milliseconds (ms).

If you’re looking for a more detailed breakdown (e.g., packet loss, jitter), many of these sites offer advanced options or downloadable reports.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like help interpreting the results or troubleshooting slow speeds!
